author: Ozvalace
quote:
Genuinely abhorrent industry practices from Rockstar, just a straight up blunt hatred of their consumers, seeing them as normal but blind cattle who will worship them in spite of it all. 
- Pushing a stripped down version of the game for an insane $80
- Releasing the standard version with all the content you would expect at an even worse price of $100
- Pushing us further towards a digital only future with no disc release as well as cheap and lazy code system that allowed thousands to illegally steal others copies
- Deceptive pay-to-see marketing that showed the game as being capable of far more than it is, with no true gameplay being shown
- Clearly buying their way into the nominations of an awards show they do not qualify for 
- Buying off and blackmailing journalists for perfect review scores with the looming threat of a blacklist

And all that just to spend 13 years making a game that is a glorified boring chore simulator with a stripped down GTA game strapped on to the side of it. The large open world has almost nothing worth actually doing making it a shallow life sim instead of enjoyable GTA game, they went way to wide for the sake of having a massive map because it sounds more impressive and that's all that apparently matters. Graphic fidelity and 'ground breaking' realism for the sake of itself, with no thought given as to how any of it improves the gameplay experience, just throw pretty colors at the consumer and they'll be too dazzled to care. Not to mention that it's riddled with so many unacceptable bugs, a terrible performance on release despite a delay to address this exact issue. The game advertises 30fps which in 2026 is abhorrent alone, except for the fact that it rarely ever hits 30fps, you'll be constantly middling around the mid 20s range feeling like a slug trailing yourself over a hill of salt. And the characters are all so bad,  Jason is a bland nothing burger yes man, Lucia is just plain annoying and verges on being blatant stereotype at times. It's a bad game but none of that matters because when you're too big to fail you can just bully and buy your way to success and the hoards of cattle will believe it anyways. The industry is relying on this game to keep it supported in dire times to show that the western games industry can still produce critical successes capable of generating billions because investors and profit are the only things that matter anymore to these people. But GTA is the exception, the normalization of this anti consumer sentiment will backfire in the face of any other series and only accelerate us further to an inevitable industry crash where hopefully everybody will lose their jobs.
